1.
Leave granted.
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3. The first appellant is the husband of the deceased and the second and third appellants are the mother-in-law and father-in-law of the deceased.
The Trial Court convicted them for the offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short IPC).
They were acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The substantive sentence for the offence punishable under Section 304B of IPC is 7 years rigorous imprisonment.
By the impugned order, the High Court has confirmed the conviction and sentence of the appellants.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants has taken us through the depositions of the prosecution witnesses and, in particular, PW No. 1(brother of the deceased), PW No. 10(mother of the deceased) and PW No. 11(father of the deceased).
He submitted that there is no evidence to show that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the appellants for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry soon before her death.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the State supported the impugned judgments by pointing out that there is more than sufficient evidence of demand for dowry and the harassment of the deceased as the demand for dowry was not complied with.
6. We have perused the evidence of the material prosecution witnesses.
It has come on record that from mid of April, 2015 to 4th June, 2015, the deceased was staying with her parents.

sentences.text:
7. Even in the Examination-in-Chief, apart from stating that dowry was demanded by appellant No.
3 (father-in-law of the deceased), PW-1 has not deposed about any cruelty or harassment of the deceased for, or in connection with, the demand for dowry.
The same is the case with the version of PW No. 10 and PW No. 11, who are the parents of the deceased.
8. Taking the examination-in-chief of the material prosecution witnesses as correct, at highest, it can be said that the prosecution has proved that there was a demand for dowry.
However, there is a complete absence of evidence of any cruelty or harassment of the deceased by the appellants for, or in connection with, the demand of dowry and that too, soon before her death.
There is no evidence of any cruelty or harassment to the deceased on account of the fact that the demand for dowry was not complied with.
Therefore, necessary ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498A of IPC are not made out.

The presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act,
1872 (for short the Evidence Act) will not come to the rescue of prosecution as the said presumption can be invoked only when it is proved that the women has been subjected by the accused to cruelty or harassment for, and in connection with, the demand for dowry soon before her death.
Therefore, the appellants could not have been convicted with the aid of Section 113B of the Evidence Act.
9. Therefore, the only conclusion which can be drawn is that the offences alleged against the appellants were not proved by the prosecution.
10. In view of the above findings, we set aside the impugned judgments and orders and direct that the appellants shall stand acquitted of the offences alleged against them.
11. The appellants be set at liberty forthwith unless they are required to be detained in connection with any other case.
12. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
